references.text: The promise of blessing for obedience to the Lord's commands is a recurring theme in Deuteronomy, where God promises to bless, love, and multiply the people who keep his statutes.
The extended text of blessings describing all the good things that will come upon Israel if they obey the voice of the Lord and keep his commandments.
Leviticus contains similar promises of blessing conditioned on obedience to God's commands and statutes.
The covenant promise at Sinai where God declares that Israel shall be his treasured people if they obey his voice and keep his covenant.
The choice between life and blessing on the one hand, and death and curse on the other, depending on obedience to the commandments.
The psalmist describes the blessed man who finds his delight in the law of the Lord and meditates on it day and night.
Wisdom literature promises blessing to those who listen to God's wisdom and walk in his ways.
James writes about the one who looks into the perfect law of freedom and holds fast to it, and is blessed in what they do.
John connects keeping God's commands with receiving what we ask from him.
